critical_concerns: Mechanism-sign mismatch: cited liquidity papers explain why illiquidity can earn premia, not why low |AC1| should deliver positive alpha.
|AC1| is an impure proxy that mixes stale pricing, reversal, volatility bursts, auction effects, and true liquidity, so the economic meaning is underidentified.
RetAutocorr already sits in a hard-fail lineage; removing Piotroski does not explain why the same crash path or left-tail exposure disappears.
Why now leans on recent 3y ICIR rank, which is ex-post hypothesis selection and weak PIT discipline for factor choice.
supporting_arguments: Single-factor smoke design is clean: it isolates the RetAutocorr sleeve before more complex mutations hide the source of failure or merit.
Microstructure/liquidity is an uncovered taxonomy bucket, so probing it with an existing DB factor has genuine research value.
No overlay and no combo keep the test falsifiable and avoid known S0/S1 violations such as timing-as-risk-management or stock-count issues.
s1_gate_items: Measure post-cost walk-forward IC/IR after KOSPI200-top and 2억원 filters; confirm edge survives 15bps turnover drag.
Decompose exposures vs size, turnover, Amihud illiquidity, beta, vol, and short-term reversal; reject if L22 is redundant.
Test left-tail concentration and crisis behavior versus STR_1636 lineage; quantify crash clustering in liquidity stress.
Audit factor timestamping: AC1 window must end before rebalance decision and exclude same-day close or future month returns.
Check sensitivity to AC1 lookback/window definition and rebalance date; reject if signal is month-end or auction artifact.
Verify effect persistence after stricter liquidity screens; prior flow-family alpha vanished when liquidity filters tightened.

kill_scenarios.scenario: In Korean risk-on rotations led by cyclicals, low |AC1| mostly selects liquid mega-cap defensives. The sleeve then adds little diversification and materially lags the opportunity set.
kill_scenarios.expected_loss: SR down 0.4-0.7; relative MDD worse by 8-12pp

kill_scenarios.scenario: The monthly factor file computes AC1 with daily returns from the rebalance month or the rebalance close itself. Backtest alpha looks clean, but live implementation cannot reproduce the signal.
kill_scenarios.expected_loss: SR collapses toward 0; live MDD 5-10pp worse

kill_scenarios.scenario: If |AC1| is mainly an illiquidity/noise proxy, the chosen negative sign buys the wrong side of the liquidity premium. After 15bps costs on an EW 20 book, any weak edge is reversed.
kill_scenarios.expected_loss: Net SR <0.2 or negative; MDD similar to or worse than benchmark by 6-10pp

weakest_assumption: Assumption: lower |AC1| is a positive tradable signal, not just a descriptor of liquid low-vol names. If wrong -> the sleeve becomes a crowded liquidity/mega-cap proxy -> expected alpha is absorbed by crowding and costs -> SR disappoints and drawdowns still appear in liquidity shocks.
design_pit_assessment: Alpha source does not inherently require ex-post knowledge, and there is no overlay or combo logic with full-sample thresholds. The PIT concern is twofold: factor selection is partly justified by recent 3y ICIR ranking, which is ex-post hypothesis picking, and AC1 timestamping is underspecified. A monthly factor built from daily returns must be explicitly lagged so the rebalance decision never uses same-day close data or returns from the forward month.
findings: REVISE. Fact: the design is simple, single-factor, and testable. Inference: the economic sign is weakly justified because the cited liquidity literature does not clearly imply that lower |AC1| should earn positive cross-sectional alpha. Speculation risk is high because |AC1| is a noisy composite proxy, and the same RetAutocorr lineage already showed catastrophic drawdown. Tighten the mechanism and PIT spec before advancing this beyond exploratory smoke status.
